title: Microprobe-driven cross-stage handoffs for kernel-adaptive prefill
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: reduce prefill stalls and improve NCCL overlap by introducing a lightweight microprobe handshake between tensor/pipeline stages. The microprobe mechanism sends short readiness probes (tiny KV-cache-prefetch-like tokens) from upstream stages to downstream executors to estimate kernel warmup needs and communication windows. Based on probe feedback the conductor will: 1) pick a kernel variant tuned for the observed sequence length distribution and device readiness, 2) opportunistically schedule NCCL collectives during predicted compute gaps, and 3) adjust microbatch handoff timing to reduce blocking during prefill and decode phases. This ticket tracks design, prototype, performance validation, and phased rollout for multi-GPU clusters (heterogeneous slot sizes).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P99 prefill latency reduced by >=10% for 8x GPU long-sequence synthetic workload compared to baseline
Measured NCCL idle time (per-step) reduced by >=15% on heterogeneous device placements in our perf harness
Kernel selection logic chooses lower-latency quantized path for >=80% of eligible requests without increasing output variance
No regressions on single-GPU latency tests and CI coverage for probe fallback paths
Can be toggled via runtime feature flag and rolled back without requiring model restart
design_notes: Microprobe format: 64B control packet piggybacked onto prefill token stream to avoid extra RPCs
Probe frequency: one probe per prefill window (configurable); trade-off between observation accuracy and overhead
Decision surface: combine device-ready-latency, observed kv-cache hit ratio, and probe RTT to pick kernel profile
Sync model: semi-asynchronous handshake with soft credits; avoids global barrier and supports opportunistic NCCL co-scheduling
Fallbacks: when probe responses delayed or missing, fall back to conservative kernel and conservative NCCL placement
Safety: probes are no-op for model outputs and are stripped before any external logs to avoid PII leakage
plan: Spike: implement probe packet + minimal responder in local multi-gpu harness (3d)
Prototype: conductor-level integration for kernel-selection hook and NCCL co-schedule hints (5d)
Perf tests: run against synthetic long-seq and production-like traces, collect NCCL idle metrics (4d)
Review: design doc + PR for kernel selection policy, iterate with Applied ML and Infra (2d)
Rollout: feature-flagged canary on dedicated pool -> metrics validate -> wider rollout
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike started. Added probe packet to local prefill path and responder stub on downstream shim. Observed median probe RTT 120us on dev 4xV100 cluster.

2026-02-27: Prototype conductor hook merged (draft PR: github.com/redwood-io/runtime/pull/3218). Basic kernel policy interface implemented; currently supports two kernel hints (fast-quant, stable-fp16).

2026-03-03: Perf harness run against long-seq synthetic trace. Initial results: NCCL idle decreased by ~7% but P99 latency unchanged. Hypothesis: probe frequency too low and kernel switch latency dominating. Added microbatch alignment adjustment to prototype.

2026-03-07: Design review with Applied ML and Infra. Feedback: add conservative safety thresholds to avoid flapping, expose probe sampling rate via per-customer config, add trace correlation id for debugging. Action: implement backoff and tracing (ENG-981724 created as follow-up).

2026-03-11: Prototype with microbatch alignment and backoff deployed to dedicated perf pool. Observed NCCL idle reduction 18% and P99 prefill latency reduction 9% on heterogeneous nodes. Preparing acceptance test run across more topologies.
2026-03-12: Open PR for instrumentation and admin flags: github.com/redwood-io/runtime/pull/3275. Requesting review from @maria-ops and @kevin-ml.
